# Godot 4.4.1 Headless Bench Server

Installs Godot Engine 4.4.1 (`Godot_v4.4.1-stable_linux.x86_64`) into `{{REPO_DIR}}`, links `/usr/local/bin/godot`, configures `/etc/godot-bench/server.cfg` and the project under `/srv/godot-bench/project`, and runs the headless HTTP server as a systemd service (`godot-bench.service`) listening on `http://godot.bench.lan:9820`.

- `ADMIN_TOKEN`: token for the `/admin` endpoint in `/etc/godot-bench/server.cfg` (generate with `openssl rand -hex 16`).

cases.prose:
# TrinityCore (3.3.5a) Server Installation

This guide installs and configures **TrinityCore** (`TDB335.24081`, commit `8938f383572a`) on Ubuntu 24.04 LTS under `{{INSTALL_DIR}}` (`/opt/trinitycore`).

What gets installed and configured:
- **Build toolchain & runtime libraries**: Clang 18, CMake 3.28, Make, GCC/G++, Boost 1.83 (`libboost-all-dev`), OpenSSL 3 (`libssl-dev`), MySQL 8.0 Server and client libraries (`mysql-server`, `libmysqlclient-dev`), Readline, Ncurses, BZip2, and `p7zip-full`.
- **Source & binaries**: TrinityCore source tree in `{{INSTALL_DIR}}/src`, compiled in `Release` mode (`-DTOOLS=0`) to produce `{{INSTALL_DIR}}/bin/authserver` and `{{INSTALL_DIR}}/bin/worldserver`.
- **Database (`mysql.service`)**: MySQL user `tcbench` and databases `tc_auth`, `tc_world`, and `tc_characters`. `tc_auth` is initialized from `sql/base/auth_database.sql` and auto-updated by `authserver`, with realm `InstallZero Bench` (`trinitycore.bench.lan:8471`) and administrator account `BENCHADMIN` (GM security level 3).
- **Systemd services**:
  - `trinity-authserver.service`: active and listening on `0.0.0.0:8470`.
  - `trinity-worldserver.service`: enabled and gated by `ConditionPathExists=/srv/trinitycore/data/dbc` (starts automatically once 3.3.5a client data files `dbc`, `maps`, `vmaps`, `mmaps` are placed in `/srv/trinitycore/data` and `TDB_full_world_335.24081_2024_08_17.sql` is available).

### Environment Variables / Secrets

- `TC_DB_PASSWORD`: Password for the MySQL user `tcbench` (if unset during install, a random 32-character hex secret is generated with `openssl rand -hex 16` and written to `/root/trinitycore-credentials.txt`).
- `TC_ADMIN_PASSWORD`: Password for the initial TrinityCore GM account `BENCHADMIN` (if unset during install, a random secret is generated and written to `/root/trinitycore-credentials.txt`).

---

cases.prose:
# Sunshine install

LizardByte Sunshine v2025.122.141614 is a self-hosted GameStream host for Moonlight. It is the Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 `.deb` from GitHub release `v2025.122.141614`, not a package from the Ubuntu archive (it is recorded only in the dpkg status database). A custom system unit runs it as user `streamer`, capturing a headless Xvfb display `:0`.

The service home and config directory is `{{REPO_DIR}}` (this host: `/srv/sunshine`). `{{INSTALL_DIR}}` is the parent of that directory.

What is running:

- `xvfb.service`: `/usr/bin/Xvfb :0 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 -nolisten tcp -ac`
- `sunshine.service`: `/usr/bin/sunshine {{REPO_DIR}}/sunshine.conf` with `HOME={{REPO_DIR}}` and `DISPLAY=:0`
- GameStream HTTP on TCP **9579** (`port` in the config; not the Sunshine default 47989)
- Web configuration UI at **https://localhost:9580** (HTTP basic auth, user `benchadmin`)
- HTTPS GameStream on TCP 9574 (`port - 5`) and RTSP on TCP 9600 (`port + 21`)

Encoding is software libx264 (`encoder = software`, `sw_preset = superfast`, `capture = x11`). An NVIDIA GPU is not required and is not installed in the guest. This machine can see an RTX 4090 through WSL, but Sunshine does not use NVENC and `nvcc` is not installed.

`/dev/uinput` on this host is `root:root` mode 0600. The packaged udev rule only sets `TAG+=uaccess`, which does not grant `streamer` access without a logged-in seat, so the log reports permission denied for the virtual mouse, keyboard, and gamepads. No extra udev rule was installed. The web UI and GameStream ports still serve.

`apps.json` is the file shipped in the package (Desktop, Low Res Desktop, Steam Big Picture). Steam is not installed. The Low Res Desktop prep-cmd calls `xrandr` on `HDMI-1`, which does not exist on this Xvfb screen; `x11-xserver-utils` is installed because that command is in the packaged apps file.

After install, open `https://<host>:9580` and sign in as `benchadmin`. Point Moonlight at port 9579.

`SUNSHINE_PASSWORD`: web UI password for user `benchadmin`. Choose it and export it before the credentials step. Do not write the value into this file. On the observed host it is stored only in `/root/sunshine-admin.txt` (mode 600, `user=benchadmin` and `password=`).

The packaged user unit `/usr/lib/systemd/user/sunshine.service` is not used. Do not enable it. The system units below pass the config path and wait for Xvfb.

steps.title: Download and extract RPCS3 Linux AppImage
steps.why: Downloads the RPCS3 Linux x64 AppImage (`v0.0.43-20336-bd179ffd`), extracts its `squashfs-root` to `{{REPO_DIR}}/AppDir`, and links `/usr/local/bin/rpcs3` to `{{REPO_DIR}}/app/AppRun`.

blocks.code: test -x "{{REPO_DIR}}/AppDir/usr/bin/rpcs3" && test -L "{{REPO_DIR}}/app" && test -f "{{REPO_DIR}}/VERSION" && test -L /usr/local/bin/rpcs3

RPCS3_VERSION="v0.0.43-20336-bd179ffd"
ASSET_NAME="rpcs3-${RPCS3_VERSION}_linux64.AppImage"
DOWNLOAD_URL="https://github.com/RPCS3/rpcs3-binaries-linux/releases/download/build-bd179ffda046c318fa4bfdc1be1cc5fd7dc5b3a2/${ASSET_NAME}"

mkdir -p "{{REPO_DIR}}"
TMP_DIR="$(mktemp -d)"
if ! curl -fsSL -o "${TMP_DIR}/${ASSET_NAME}" "${DOWNLOAD_URL}"; then
  RELEASE_JSON="$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/RPCS3/rpcs3-binaries-linux/releases/latest)"
  ASSET_NAME="$(printf '%s' "${RELEASE_JSON}" | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name | endswith("_linux64.AppImage")) | .name' | head -n1)"
  DOWNLOAD_URL="$(printf '%s' "${RELEASE_JSON}" | jq -r '.assets[] | select(.name | endswith("_linux64.AppImage")) | .browser_download_url' | head -n1)"
  RPCS3_VERSION="$(printf '%s' "${ASSET_NAME}" | sed -E 's/^rpcs3-(.*)_linux64\.AppImage$/\1/')"
  curl -fsSL -o "${TMP_DIR}/${ASSET_NAME}" "${DOWNLOAD_URL}"
fi

chmod +x "${TMP_DIR}/${ASSET_NAME}"
(cd "${TMP_DIR}" && "./${ASSET_NAME}" --appimage-extract >/dev/null)
rm -rf "{{REPO_DIR}}/AppDir"
mv "${TMP_DIR}/squashfs-root" "{{REPO_DIR}}/AppDir"
ln -sfn ./AppDir "{{REPO_DIR}}/app"
cat > "{{REPO_DIR}}/VERSION" <<EOF
${RPCS3_VERSION}
asset=${ASSET_NAME}
EOF
ln -sfn "{{REPO_DIR}}/app/AppRun" /usr/local/bin/rpcs3
rm -rf "${TMP_DIR}"
test -x "{{REPO_DIR}}/app/AppRun" && test -x "{{REPO_DIR}}/AppDir/usr/bin/rpcs3" && test -f "{{REPO_DIR}}/VERSION" && test -L /usr/local/bin/rpcs3

steps.why: Pre-populates the headless RPCS3 configuration under `/srv/rpcs3/config/rpcs3/config/config.yml` and generates the `x11vnc` password files in `/etc/rpcs3` (provide `RPCS3_VNC_PASSWORD` in the environment to set a custom password, otherwise a random password is generated and saved to `/etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt`).

blocks.code: test -f /srv/rpcs3/config/rpcs3/config/config.yml && test -s /etc/rpcs3/vncpasswd && test -s /etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt

install -d -m 0755 -o rpcs3 -g rpcs3 /srv/rpcs3/config/rpcs3/config
cat > /srv/rpcs3/config/rpcs3/config/config.yml <<'EOF'
Core:

Video:
  Renderer: "Null"
  Frame limit: 30
Audio:

EOF

if [ ! -s /etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt ]; then
  VNC_PASS="${RPCS3_VNC_PASSWORD:-$(tr -dc 'A-Za-z0-9' </dev/urandom | head -c 8)}"
  printf '%s\n' "${VNC_PASS}" > /etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt
  chmod 0600 /etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt
fi
x11vnc -storepasswd "$(head -n1 /etc/rpcs3/vnc-password.txt)" /etc/rpcs3/vncpasswd
chmod 0600 /etc/rpcs3/vncpasswd

steps.title: Configure and start RPCS3, Xvfb, x11vnc, and noVNC services
steps.why: Creates and starts the systemd units `rpcs3-xvfb.service`, `rpcs3.service`, `rpcs3-vnc.service`, and `rpcs3-novnc.service` so RPCS3 runs persistently on `:1` and is accessible via noVNC on port 8740.

blocks.code: systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-xvfb.service && systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3.service && systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-vnc.service && systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-novnc.service

cat > /etc/systemd/system/rpcs3-xvfb.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=Virtual X display :1 for RPCS3
After=network.target

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/Xvfb :1 -screen 0 1600x900x24 -nolisten tcp
Restart=always
RestartSec=3

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

cat > /etc/systemd/system/rpcs3.service <<EOF
[Unit]
Description=RPCS3 PlayStation 3 emulator (headless on Xvfb :1)
After=rpcs3-xvfb.service
Requires=rpcs3-xvfb.service

[Service]
User=rpcs3
Group=rpcs3
WorkingDirectory=/srv/rpcs3
Environment=DISPLAY=:1
Environment=HOME=/srv/rpcs3
Environment=XDG_CONFIG_HOME=/srv/rpcs3/config
Environment=QT_QPA_PLATFORM=xcb
Environment=LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
Environment=TZ=Europe/Berlin
ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 2
ExecStart={{REPO_DIR}}/app/AppRun
Restart=always
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

cat > /etc/systemd/system/rpcs3-vnc.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=x11vnc export of RPCS3 display :1
After=rpcs3-xvfb.service
Requires=rpcs3-xvfb.service

[Service]
ExecStartPre=/bin/sleep 2
ExecStart=/usr/bin/x11vnc -display :1 -rfbport 8741 -localhost -rfbauth /etc/rpcs3/vncpasswd -forever -shared -noxdamage
Restart=always
RestartSec=3

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

cat > /etc/systemd/system/rpcs3-novnc.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=noVNC web client for RPCS3 on port 8740
After=rpcs3-vnc.service
Wants=rpcs3-vnc.service

[Service]
ExecStart=/usr/bin/websockify --web /usr/share/novnc 8740 localhost:8741
Restart=always
RestartSec=3

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
EOF

systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now rpcs3-xvfb.service rpcs3.service rpcs3-vnc.service rpcs3-novnc.service

systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-xvfb.service && \
systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3.service && \
systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-vnc.service && \
systemctl is-active --quiet rpcs3-novnc.service && \
ss -tln | grep -q ':8741 ' && \
ss -tln | grep -q ':8740 ' && \
curl -fsSI http://127.0.0.1:8740/vnc.html >/dev/null

# NetBox 4.7.3 install

This document records the procedure used to install NetBox 4.7.3 on this Ubuntu 24.04 LTS machine. NetBox is installed in `/opt/netbox` with Python 3.12, a virtual environment (`/opt/netbox/venv`), and the application directory (`/opt/netbox/netbox`). It uses PostgreSQL 16 as its database and Redis 7 as its cache backend. Nginx proxies HTTP requests to the Gunicorn WSGI service on port 8001, and a systemd request queue worker (`netbox-rq.service`) consumes Redis queue jobs.

cases.prose:
# rl-roboracer install

This document describes how to install the rl‑roboracer stack on a clean Windows 11 machine. The stack is delivered as a set of Docker Compose services that run a ROS server, a MongoDB database, a Unity simulation controller, a dashboard, and a training brain. The only system‑level requirement is Docker Desktop with WSL 2 and NVIDIA GPU support. All runtime code is contained in the Docker images, so no additional Python or Node installations are needed.

The install proceeds in the following order:
1. Install Docker Desktop with WSL 2 and NVIDIA Container Toolkit.
2. Verify the NVIDIA driver and Docker GPU integration.
3. Build or pull the required Docker images.
4. Create a minimal `.env` file with placeholder values.
5. Bring up the stack with `docker compose`.
6. Verify that the services are running and that the dashboard is reachable.

Feel free to adjust the `.env` values to point to your own data directories or credentials.
